title: Architect a modular tone system and variable elevation ratio for dense components
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Our current token set mixes implementation-focused surface values with semantic intents which makes consistent color, elevation and radius application across dense controls (tables, compact lists, action bars) error-prone. Designers and engineers repeatedly duplicate near-identical styles leading to maintenance debt and inconsistent accessibility across small-view components.

Goal: Define a modular tone system (semantic buckets + configurable ramps) and a paired variable elevation ratio so dense components can adopt compact footprints while preserving contrast and perceived depth. The system should be:
- Semantic-first (surface, interactive, emphasis, decorative) with clear aliasing to implementation tokens.
- Responsive: support compact/regular/roomy density modes via a single density token set.
- Programmable: expose a small set of primitive tokens (hue anchors, neutral anchors, tone steps, elevation ratio) that can be computed into derived tokens by the build tooling.
- Accessible: meet WCAG 2.2 contrast targets for primary/secondary text at small sizes and for key controls in compact mode.

Scope: color palette anchors (4 hue anchors + neutral), typography scale adjustments for small-size legibility, spacing/radius primitives (touch-aware radius scale with variable token), shadow/elevation defined as layered soft+directional geometry with a variable ratio (e.g., 1 : 1.6 : 2.6) that can be tuned per density.

Deliverables:
- Token spec doc (Confluence) with migration mapping from old tokens to new semantic tokens and examples for tables, buttons, chips and charts.
- Figma token library and component variants for compact/regular densities.
- Migration guide and codemods for frontend repo to alias legacy tokens to new derived tokens.
- QA checklist and perf/visual regression test plan.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Semantic tokens defined and mapped to existing components in Figma with examples for dense table rows and compact toolbar.
2) New elevation layers implemented in a small demo page and visual diff < 2 failing pixels on critical paths vs approved reference for both densities.
3) Contrast checks automated for primary/secondary text sizes in both density modes.
4) Migration plan and codemod PR opened in design-system repo (link in comments).

Constraints and trade-offs:
- We prefer a small set of primitives to avoid exploding the token surface area.
- Some legacy product surfaces will keep legacy tokens during a multi-release migration window; provide aliasing strategy.

Notes: this ticket focuses on the token architecture and design artifacts; engineering implementation of tokens in CSS/JS variables will be a follow-up ticket coordinated with ENG.
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Kickoff — scoped the token primitives and confirmed the compact density target (row height 32px for dense lists). Added initial Figma board and Confluence outline: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/TOKENS-2026-compact

2026-03-11 Priya Kapoor: Pulled in accessibility team for early contrast guidance; target for primary small text set to 4.5:1 where possible. Asked engineering to evaluate runtime token computation feasibility (CSS variables + small script).

2026-03-12 Design critique: Decided on 4 hue anchors (brand, success, warning, danger) plus a neutral anchor; each anchor exposes 6 tone steps (10/25/40/60/80/95) — agreed to use HSL ramping with perceptual adjustments. Action: Maya to author precise HSL anchors.

2026-03-13 Engineering sync (ENG-20124): Backend & serving team confirmed codemod approach for token aliasing is feasible; suggested using a migration layer that maps semantic token names to legacy CSS vars for a 2-release deprecation. Assigned follow-up ENG ticket. Link to PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/design-system/pull/

2026-03-14 Visual QA: Created demo pages for compact and regular density. Early feedback: shadows in compact mode appear too hard — lowered directional shadow alpha and increased blur for soft layer. Updated elevation ratio draft from 1:2:4 to 1:1.6:2.6 for perceived continuity.

2026-03-15 Maya Chen: Uploaded Figma library v0.2 with component variants and token page. Added migration mapping spreadsheet and codemod TODOs. Next: finalize token names, write Confluence spec, and open migration PRs.
